_provenance.source_release: RFC 4231 (December 2005), IETF -- Identifiers and Test Vectors for HMAC-SHA-224/256/384/512
_provenance.producer: Python 3.12 hmac + hashlib (OpenSSL-backed), cross-checked against an independent from-scratch ipad/opad HMAC construction for every algorithm below (both agree exactly for all 11)
_provenance.note: RFC 4231 §4.2 Test Case 1 (SHA2-224/256/384/512); self-computed extension of the identical construction for SHA-1/SHA2-512-224/SHA2-512-256/SHA3-224/256/384/512, which RFC 4231 does not define -- Closes a real coverage gap: commit 58be5cb4 fixed a kMacMechTable bug (src/lib/SoftHSM_sign.cpp) where minKeyBytes for every plain-digest HMAC mechanism was set to that digest's own output length, so MacSignInit/MacVerifyInit rejected any key shorter than the digest with CKR_KEY_SIZE_RANGE. The bug shipped undetected because every curated ACVP-Server sample in this directory's other hmac*.json files uses a key >=121 bytes (hmac_test.json's is 228) -- none of them exercise a shorter-than-digest key, which is exactly the condition the bug hinged on. RFC 2104 places no lower bound on an HMAC key; RFC 4231 SS4.2 Test Case 1 is the standard's own canonical vector proving this: a 20-byte key (0x0b x20) against "Hi There", deliberately shorter than SHA-384/512's digest output. This file's SHA2-256 group matches, byte for byte, the literal expected value already hardcoded in openmls-provider/lib/tests/integration.rs's hmac_sha256_known_answer (same key/message/hash: b0344c61d8db38535ca8afceaf0bf12b881dc200c9833da726e9376c2e32cff7) -- that native-Rust-engine test (via PKCS#11) is what originally caught this bug; this file brings the same short-key coverage to the wasm harness (C++ engine, via raw PKCS#11 calls from Node/JS) as a genuine second, independent-runtime cross-check, not a duplicate. Uses each mechanism's plain (non-_GENERAL, exact-length) form -- RFC 4231's published MACs are full untruncated digests, unlike the truncated SP 800-107 samples the sibling hmac*.json files use with CKM_*_HMAC_GENERAL. Note: the SHA-1 group's key length (20 bytes) equals SHA-1's own digest length exactly -- it satisfies (does not violate) the old buggy minKeyBytes=digestLen check, so it does not by itself prove the regression the way the other 10 groups do; it is included only for HMAC-SHA-1 plain-mechanism KAT coverage, which this harness otherwise has none of.
